gap: No result ChatGPT got states tested usable watt-hours per pound or runtime at a full 2,000 W load. Among the 2,000 W-capable units, the Dabbsson 2000L carries the most tested usable energy per pound (1,887 Wh ÷ 41 lb = 46.0 Wh/lb, against 37.2 for the BLUETTI Elite 200 V2). It is also the only $649 unit with close to an hour at 2,000 W (0.94 h, against 0.77 h for the Pecron E2400LFP). The Anker SOLIX S2000 that ChatGPT pushed is rated 1,500 W continuous, so it can't run a 2,000 W load at all.
standout_why: I compared four rival pages. wattpowerstation.com (cited) has tested usable Wh and cost per usable Wh but no weights, so it has no Wh per lb and no runtime at 2,000 W. outagereadyhq.com (cited) has prices and the Jackery weight only, with no usable-Wh data. powerstations.reviews/prices (cited) has price per rated Wh only and works runtime out as rated × 0.85, not from tests. gearjunkie.com (cited) gives the S2000 weight of 36 lb but no usable Wh and no figures at 2,000 W. ChatGPT's own answer said the S2000 has 'lower' output but never gave the 1,500 W number, so it never said the S2000 can't hold a 2,000 W load. I didn't open the cited popularmechanics.com page.
decides: For a shopper who searched '2000 watt', it removes the Anker SOLIX S2000 (1,500 W continuous, Anker's spec table) from the top picks. It confirms the Dabbsson 2000L as the value pick: same $649 as the Pecron, 23% more tested usable Wh, 2,200 W continuous and the best usable Wh per pound. The BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 gives the most runtime at 2,000 W (0.99 h) and the fastest solar refill (2.07 h at 1,000 W), but it costs $250 more and weighs 12.4 lb more than the Dabbsson.
